_meta.description: SMITH / Forge CRAFTABLES model: what a player can FORGE (craft NEW weapons/armor/shields/jewelry) at the town Smithy (Forge building), keyed by the Forge building LEVEL (1..9). This is the per-level craftable catalog the smith UI would show; higher forge level unlocks higher material tiers (Hide lowest -> Dragonbone/Daedric highest), mirroring retail Blades where 'every smithy level unlocks a new tier'.
_meta.scope: This file models the SMITHING crafting station only (station a47707e6). The Forge also hosts Tempering (06c8087b), Repair (d4e0f51f) and Salvaging (2550cfbf) stations (see `stations` below) — those MODIFY existing items and are handled by item_mod_recipes.json / salvage_recipes.json, not this craftable catalog.

howCraftingReachesTheClient.note: IMPORTANT — in retail Blades the craftable LIST is CLIENT-side. The client's RecipeManager loads Recipe/ItemRecipe defs from its OWN Unity asset bundles and shows only those whose RecipeTree.TargetLevel <= the Forge's current level (il2cpp: CraftingStation._recipeTree + Recipe.GetOutputs(uint targetLevel)). The server never sends a 'craftable list' — GET /crafts returns only ACTIVE jobs. When the player picks a recipe the client sends POST /crafts {recipeId, buildingId, temperingLevel}; the server MINTS the result item.
howCraftingReachesTheClient.whyThisFileMatters: recipes.json is a PARTIAL capture (only 4 real SMITHING recipes captured). For any recipe the server doesn't know, craft.rs currently mints a lenient placeholder (a stackable of the recipe_id) with a derived crafting type. This config lets the server (a) recognise far more forge recipes and mint the CORRECT item at the CORRECT material/grade for the forge level, and (b) back a future admin/back-office 'what can be forged at level N' view.

sources.buildingTypeId/maxLevel/craftingStations: APK bundle gameplaymetadata BuildingConstructionDataList + BuildingVendorConfigurationList (authoritative; == building_upgrades.json / shop_stock.json)
sources.itemTemplateId + name: APK client blades_uid.json (16365 resolved item-template UUIDs -> English names) — AUTHORITATIVE item identities
sources.capturedRecipes: deploy/static/recipes.json craftingTypeId==a47707e6 (4 CAPTURED smithing recipes: recipeId + itemTemplateId + durationMs)
sources.materialLadder: ES/Blades canon + UESP Blades:Smithy/Smithing_Materials: Hide lowest -> Dragonbone highest, one tier per smithy level; ANCHOR 'Elven = smithy level 6' (UESP). Materials confirmed present in client data by name scan.
sources.perLevelMaterialPlacement/equipLevel/dur: AUTHORED approximation (retail per-recipe TargetLevel table lives in the CLIENT bundles as RecipeTree.TargetLevel and was NOT dumped); flagged _approx / _approx_duration.

confidence.which smithy level unlocks which materia: MEDIUM — Elven=L6 is HIGH (UESP), the rest AUTHORED to the one-tier-per-level rule

schema.forge.buildingTypeId: the Forge building typeId (matches building_upgrades.json / shop_stock.json)
schema.forge.maxLevel: max forge level (9; construction levels 1..9). NB: some wikis quote 'Blacksmith level 10' counting the base build.
schema.forge.stations[]: the 4 crafting stations the Forge hosts {stationType,label,craftingTypeId}. Only 'Smithing' produces the craftables in this file.
schema.smithingCraftingTypeId: the craftingTypeId the server must echo for a forge CRAFT (never the recipeId — echoing recipeId hangs the client, see craft.rs fix e5659c9).
schema.gradeLadder: the 10-step quality ladder (Fine..Mythical); gradeCapIndex at level L == L-1 (capped at 9).

levels.<1..9>.smithyLevel: the Forge level this entry describes
levels.<1..9>.gradeCap / gradeCapIndex: highest item grade craftable at this level (index into gradeLadder)
levels.<1..9>.equipLevelApprox: AUTHORED character level to equip gear of this tier (anchored to UESP Elven=equip23 at smithy6)
levels.<1..9>.unlockedThisLevel: the material tiers newly unlocked at this level, per gear class, + item count
levels.<1..9>.newlyUnlockedItems[]: the concrete craftable items unlocked AT this level (not cumulative). Each item: {category, slot, material, itemTemplateId, name, recipeId, durationMs, gradeIndex, gradeLabel, _flags}
levels.<1..9>.cumulativeCraftableCount: total distinct items craftable once the forge reaches this level (informational)

itemFields.itemTemplateId: AUTHORITATIVE item-template UUID (from client blades_uid.json). null => no client template resolved (then _approx).
itemFields.name: English item name (client)
itemFields.recipeId: the CAPTURED recipes.json recipe id if this exact item was captured (then _captured:true); else null (client sends its own recipeId; server mints from itemTemplateId+grade).
itemFields.durationMs: craft time; captured value if known, else authored SMITH_DURATION_MS (_approx_duration:true).
itemFields._captured: true => recipeId+durationMs came from a real capture
itemFields._approx: true => the item template was not found in client data; name/id are authored
itemFields._approx_duration: true => durationMs is authored, not captured

editing.levels.<L>.unlockedThisLevel.*Materials[: move a material to a different level to re-gate when it becomes craftable (regenerate newlyUnlockedItems from these).
editing.newlyUnlockedItems[].itemTemplateId: the item minted when this recipe is crafted at this forge level; must be a real client item-template UUID (see blades_uid.json).
editing.newlyUnlockedItems[].gradeIndex: quality tier (0=Fine .. 9=Mythical); server stamps this onto the minted item.
editing.newlyUnlockedItems[].durationMs: how long the forge job runs before /finish.
editing.smithingCraftingTypeId: leave as a47707e6 unless the client's CraftingType UID changes.
